hints.title: Longest Subsequence Extension Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the longest strictly increasing subsequence requires evaluating which earlier elements can extend a valid sequence. How can maintaining the smallest possible tail values for subsequences of each length allow deciding optimal placements in logarithmic time per element?

hints.title: Monotonic Tails Invariant
hints.text: Storing the smallest ending value for each subsequence length creates a strictly increasing array of tails, where each new number either extends the longest length or lowers a tail value.

hints.title: Patience Sorting Binary Search Procedure
hints.text: Initialize an empty list of tails. For each number in the array, locate its insertion point in tails via half-interval comparison. If the number is greater than all existing elements, append it. Otherwise, replace the element at the insertion point with the current number. Return the length of tails.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array nums (1 <= N <= 2500)
complexity.notes: Binary searches the tails array for each of the N elements.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Classic O(N^2) pairwise dynamic programming checks every previous element, which is too slow for large inputs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Patience sorting maintains monotonic tails array in O(N) space and speeds up searches to O(N log N).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining patience sorting concept, bisect_left insertion invariant, recognizing final length equals tails array length.
